summary: Wii Sports entries from the prepared 1000-title candidate queue, researched for Sami's fidelity-first archive route.

entries.title: Wii Sports

emulation.emulator: Dolphin only after real Wii Remote input is verified
emulation.notes: Prefer original Wii hardware if input authenticity is more important than upscaled capture.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Original Wii hardware authenticity, or Dolphin upscaling with real Wii Remote controls

primary.version: Original Wii release with real Wii Remote controls
primary.why: Wii Sports is built around Wii Remote motion input. The original Wii release is the content and control authority; emulation can improve image capture, but only if real Wii Remote behavior is preserved.
primary.how_to_play: Use original Wii hardware for the control-authentic run, or Dolphin with a real Wii Remote/sensor setup only after input behavior is verified. Treat Wii Sports Club as a separate HD remake/variant, not the replacement for the original.

all_releases.fidelity: Original motion-control sports package with Tennis, Baseball, Bowling, Golf, and Boxing.
all_releases.reason: primary: content and input authority for the original game.

all_releases.platform: Wii Sports Club on Wii U
all_releases.fidelity: HD Wii U remake/service route with online features historically attached.
all_releases.reason: skip: useful comparison route, but not the original Wii Sports entry and Wii U online service is no longer a current completeness advantage.

all_releases.fidelity: Later successor with different sports mix and Switch controls.
all_releases.reason: skip: separate game, not a version of Wii Sports.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Dolphin can improve image fidelity, but the archive route should not sacrifice real Wii Remote motion behavior.

entries.remaster_caveats: Wii Sports Club is a Wii U remake/variant with a different service context. Nintendo Switch Sports is a separate successor.

entries.title: Wii Sports Resort
entries.definitive_edition: Original Wii release with Wii MotionPlus/Wii Remote Plus

emulation.notes: Use original controllers/passthrough and document calibration if emulating.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Original Wii or Wii U backward compatibility with Wii MotionPlus

primary.version: Original Wii release with Wii MotionPlus / Wii Remote Plus
primary.why: Wii Sports Resort is built around Wii MotionPlus, and its motion-control feel is the main artifact. Original Wii or Wii U backward compatibility with the real controller setup is the best archive route.
primary.how_to_play: Use a Wii or Wii U in backward-compatibility mode with Wii MotionPlus or Wii Remote Plus. Record controller model, calibration, sensor bar/display setup, players, sport list/progress, and any Dolphin comparison settings.

secondary.what_to_play: Use only if original hardware capture is unavailable.
secondary.why: MotionPlus calibration and controller authenticity are central to the experience.

all_releases.fidelity: Original hardware and Wii MotionPlus route.
all_releases.reason: primary: intended controller and motion experience.
primary: valid hardware route with the same controller requirement.

all_releases.fidelity: Emulated route with controller passthrough/configuration caveats.
all_releases.reason: secondary: useful capture route only if real hardware is unavailable.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Real MotionPlus hardware is more important than resolution or emulator convenience.

entries.remaster_caveats: Record controller, calibration, and capture setup; motion feel can vary by hardware.
